headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,280 AS OCTOBER HIKE ODDS HIT 70% — Brief $4,349 Recovery Fails; Dollar Near 2-Month High, Silver Firms at $64
snippet: Gold closed the week around $4,280 on September 25-26, down more than 1% for the week and failing to hold its brief $4,349 recovery level, as CME FedWatch priced an October rate hike at nearly 70% probability and a December hike at 95%. The Fed's September hike to 3.75%-4.00% initially weighed on bullion, but real-yield dynamics and fiscal risk brought buyers in within 48 hours before the dollar reasserted itself near a two-month high. Silver firmed to $64 per ounce on Friday after two days of losses. Gold remains roughly 24% off its January $5,595 record; producer margins at these levels remain historically elevated, sustaining cash generation throughout the pullback.

headline: COT REPORT: GOLD FUNDS HOLD 144,747 NET LONG — Pace of Buying at 97th Percentile, Level at 70th; Silver Net Positions Contract
snippet: The September 25 Commitment of Traders report for gold, silver and the US Dollar index shows managed money holding 144,747 net long COMEX gold contracts — the 70th percentile of the historical positioning range — while the pace of that buildup over the prior 13 weeks ranks at the 97th percentile of all comparable stretches in the 20-year record, up 16% over 30 days. Silver net positions contracted on the week. The fast-but-not-extreme positioning suggests fund managers are committed but have not reached crowded extremes that historically precede sharp corrections. Steel led all base metals in new speculative bets in an otherwise lower week for commodity funds.

headline: NIGER RESETS URANIUM TERMS — Atomic Eagle Gives State 40% of Madaouela; Keeps Operational Control; $40M Funding Backstop Agreed
snippet: Niger and Australia's Atomic Eagle signed a new agreement on September 23 resetting the terms of the Madaouela 1 uranium project near Arlit: Niger's stake doubles from 20% to 40% (15% free-carried plus 25% funded), while Atomic Eagle retains 60% and full operational control. The company agreed to cover up to $40 million of Niger's future funding obligations plus two $5 million milestone payments at permit and construction start. Atomic Eagle's CEO expects the deal to unlock renewed Western financing interest, with the US government having separately committed US$414.2 million conditionally to a rival uranium project in the same country — signalling that bilateral partners are competing to secure a Sahel uranium supply chain outside Chinese and Russian influence.

headline: VIKING MINES +25% ON NEVADA TUNGSTEN HITS — 18m @ 0.42% WO₃, 13m @ 0.46% at Linka; US Domestic Critical Mineral Supply Story Emerges
snippet: Viking Mines (ASX: VKA) surged 25% on September 24 after RC drilling at the historic Linka Mine in Nevada returned tungsten intercepts of 18m at 0.42% WO3 and 13m at 0.46% WO3 from holes LKRC0005 and LKRC0006 — grades consistent with the mine's 1950s operational period — with shallower holes confirming near-surface mineralisation up-dip. The 20-hole maiden RC programme has now defined thick scheelite zones with an 86% drill-hole success rate. Drilling resumes mid-October after a contractor break; the geological model is being updated in the interim. Tungsten's critical role in military hardware and high-temperature industrial applications has attracted US government backing for Nevada domestic supply programs, making Linka a timely strategic asset.

headline: PROSPECTOR TESS ZONE: 24.2 g/t AU OVER 3.5m IN POLYMETALLIC ENVELOPE — Hole ML26-46 Adds Third High-Grade Zone; 25,000m Program Wrapping Up
snippet: Prospector Metals Corp (TSXV: PPP) reported that diamond drill hole ML26-46 at the TESS Zone in the ML Project, Yukon, returned multiple high-grade intervals including 24.17 g/t Au, 31.64 g/t Ag and 1.62% Cu over 3.5 metres and 5.05 g/t Au, 29.25 g/t Ag and 1.16% Cu over 27.35 metres — adding a third distinct high-grade zone to the discovery. The fully funded 25,000-metre 2026 campaign using three drill rigs has now completed 88 holes, with earlier headline hole ML31 returning 44m at 13.79 g/t Au, 38.08 g/t Ag and 1.89% Cu. Preliminary metallurgical work is underway, with initial cyanide bottle-roll tests on the TESS and Phoenix gold-copper zones expected once all 2026 assays are finalised.

headline: CATL JIANXIAWO BACK ON CARE & MAINTENANCE — EIA Revoked Again; Benchmark Cuts 2026 LCE Forecast by 30,500t; Restart Now Q4 or 2027
snippet: China's largest lithium mine by capacity — CATL's Jianxiawo lepidolite operation in Jiangxi — is back on care and maintenance after the Yichun Ecology and Environment Bureau revoked its environmental assessment approval following more than 70 formal tailings-pond complaints. CATL secured a safety production permit on June 29 but bypassed an unresolved EIA dispute in its informal restart, triggering the revocation. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence cut its 2026 mined output forecast for Jianxiawo from 62,500 to 32,000 tonnes LCE, with a new environmental review process extending the restart timeline into Q4 2026 or 2027. The reduction threatens to flip analysts' projected 2026 global lithium surplus into a deficit.

headline: LITHIUM STOCKS SLIDE AS LIT ETF FALLS 1.09% — Albemarle -4.60%, SQM -2.84% on Sept 25; Ganfeng Revenue Triples, Tianqi 49x Profit in H1
snippet: The Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF (LIT) fell 1.09% on September 25, with Albemarle dropping 4.60% and SQM losing 2.84%, as the Western lithium producer complex extended its weekly decline. The selloff stands in contrast to Chinese producers reporting strong H1 2026 results: Ganfeng Lithium swung to profit with revenue nearly tripling, while Tianqi Lithium's profit surged 49-fold year-on-year as revenues soared 153% — a sharp divergence reflecting low-cost Chinese producers recovering on spot price gains versus higher-cost Western peers still facing margin pressure. The bifurcation sharpens the strategic argument for supply-chain diversification among non-Chinese lithium producers.

headline: EQUINOX-ORLA CLOSES: US$18.5B NORTH AMERICAN GOLD GIANT BORN — 1.1M Oz Across Six Mines; Clear Path to 1.9M Oz by 2030
snippet: Equinox Gold and Orla Mining have completed their US$18.5 billion business combination, creating a new North American senior gold producer targeting approximately 1.1 million ounces of annual production across six operating mines in Canada, the United States, Mexico, and Nicaragua. Orla shareholders received 1.00 Equinox share per Orla share held, with existing Equinox shareholders retaining approximately 67% of the combined company. The deal is anchored by three cornerstone Canadian assets — Greenstone (Ontario), Valentine (Newfoundland), and Musselwhite (Ontario) — and carries a fully funded growth pipeline toward 1.9 million ounces annually. Equinox CEO Darren Hall leads the combined entity, with Orla's Jason Simpson becoming president.

headline: COPPER HOLDS NEAR RECORD $6.70/LB — Goldman Projects 8.2M-Tonne Gap by 2030; Escondida Phased Restart Slow; 600,000t Gone From 2026 Supply
snippet: COMEX copper held near $6.70 per pound in late September, within range of the September 8 intraday record of $6.83, as supply disruptions continue to provide structural support. Disruptions at Grasberg and Kamoa-Kakula have removed an estimated 600,000 tonnes from 2026 production, while BHP's Escondida — the world's largest copper mine — remains in a phased restart following the September 23 fatality with full resumption timeline uncertain. Goldman Sachs projects an 8.2 million tonne copper supply gap by 2030 driven by data centre and electrification demand outpacing a capex cycle running years behind schedule. Analysts note owning copper miners provides superior leverage to the structural deficit over physical copper exposure.

headline: GOLD: SELLOFF OR BREAKOUT? — Vermeulen Sees Bull Flag or Bear Bounce; Lower Highs, Lower Lows Persist Despite $4,300 Hold
snippet: Technical analyst Chris Vermeulen warns that gold's 150-day moving average remains in a declining trend with the metal continuing to print lower highs and lower lows despite holding above $4,300. The recent rally from the post-Fed-hike low could develop into a bull flag launching a major new gold rally — or it could prove to be another bear-market bounce that ultimately resolves lower. Vermeulen notes investment demand will remain the primary driver per the World Gold Council, but cautions that the short-term trend is technically bearish from pure price-action standpoint. The analysis has significant implications for junior mining investors who use gold's near-term trajectory to size positions.

headline: CHINA SILVER IMPORTS HIT 790+ TONNES IN EARLY 2026 — Sixth Straight Supply Deficit Year; Silver Equities Still Lag the Metal's Price Rally
snippet: China imported more than 790 tonnes of silver in the first months of 2026, extending what the Silver Institute projects as the sixth consecutive year of structural supply deficit as industrial and investment demand continues to outpace mined and recycled output. Silvercorp Metals temporarily suspended operations at its Ying and GC mines in China to comply with new national safety regulations, with production expected to drop 40-50% at Ying through September. Silver spot held near $64 per ounce despite dollar strength and hawkish Fed expectations, sustaining the metal's premium over mining equity valuations that analysts argue still have not fully priced in the multi-year structural demand shift underpinning the bull case.

headline: GOLD MINERS AT 'POTENTIALLY EXPLOSIVE NEW PHASE' — Record Margins Above $4,300; Producers Flush With Free Cash Flow; Junior Leverage Underpriced
snippet: A September 24 market commentary argues gold mining stocks are entering a potentially explosive new phase as major producers report record free cash flow margins at gold prices above $4,300 per ounce. Newmont's global mine portfolio, ongoing buybacks, and strong dividends make it compelling for pure gold exposure, while Coeur Mining reported record revenue and near-27% margins. The analysis highlights that junior exploration companies provide significantly underpriced leverage to the gold price: historically, juniors with quality assets multiply gains relative to seniors when institutional money rotates down the cap scale — and that rotation has not yet fully materialised in the current cycle despite gold holding at historically high absolute levels.
